decided: Close the local/CI step-list gap by ADDING the two missing steps to the local gate, never by removing them from CI. Five coordinated edits: (1) repo.yaml's verify.core gains `./scripts/ci-go.sh vuln` and `./scripts/ci-go.sh lint` so the local scope is the same six commands, in the same order, as the CI 'core checks' job. (2) scripts/ci-go.sh gains one pinned GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION (v2.13.1, the version CI already installs) and resolves the linter ONCE before the module loop: a golangci-lint on PATH whose `version --short` equals the pin is used as-is (that is CI's checksum-verified binary); anything else -- absent, or present at a different version -- falls back to `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@<pin>`, exactly the pattern GOVULNCHECK_VERSION already uses, with one loud stderr line saying which path was taken. The pin, not the machine, decides what `lint` means. (3) .github/workflows/ci.yml keeps its checksum-verified release-binary install (fast and content-addressed on a cold runner) but derives the version from `./scripts/ci-go.sh lint-version`, a new non-module mode, so the pin has exactly one home; if the hardcoded sha256 and ci-go.sh's pin ever separate, the sha256sum step fails loudly rather than linting with a different analyzer. (4) repo.yaml's 'can never drift apart' comment is rewritten to separate the two axes it conflated: MODULE discovery (always was true) and the STEP LIST (false until this change; now stated as the invariant both lists must hold). (5) the three places that restate the core-check list -- .github/pull_request_template.md, .warden/skills-policy.md's Verify section, and CONTRIBUTING.md's Commands section -- are corrected in the same PR under ADR-0008 clause 4.
why: The gap is not theoretical: PR #90 burned a full CI round trip on two staticcheck SA1019 hits that no local step could surface, because `go vet` does not run that analysis. The deliver protocol tells every agent that `warden verify --scope core` plus `warden review` is 'exactly what CI will say'; for two of six steps that sentence was false, and an agent that believes it ships a red PR. The only fix that makes the sentence true is running the missing analysis locally. The blocker was that golangci-lint is not installed here, so a naive `lint` step would fail with 'command not found' -- a local gate red for a missing tool rather than a real finding, which is worse than the gap. That blocker is now measured, not guessed: on this tree, `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.13.1 run ./...` across all 18 discovered modules completes in 37s and reports 0 issues, and `./scripts/ci-go.sh vuln` completes in 30s and reports no vulnerabilities. Roughly 70s added to a local gate that already runs build+test across 18 modules is a fair price for removing a class of CI round trip. CI keeps the release binary because ci.yml's own comment records the evidence against source builds THERE ('network-fragile (sumdb stream errors) and slow') -- that evidence is about a cold GitHub runner with no module cache, not about a developer machine where the build is paid once and cached. Preferring a PATH binary only at the exact pin, and otherwise falling back to the pin, means the two environments can disagree about SPEED but never about ANALYSIS.
cost_if_wrong: Bounded and reversible. Worst realistic case: the local gate gets ~70s slower, and the first lint run on a cold module cache costs minutes while `go run` builds the linter (one time, then cached -- the same cost govulncheck already imposes and the repo already accepts). Second case: a future Go toolchain that golangci-lint v2.13.1 will not build under. That fails LOUD -- a non-zero `go run` build error propagating through ci-go.sh's `fail=1` -- rather than silently skipping the check, so it is fail-closed in the direction the platform requires; the remedy is bumping one pinned version. Third case: a contributor with a different golangci-lint on PATH silently gets the slower fallback path; the script prints why, so it is visible, not silent. Nothing here weakens a check: every step CI runs still runs in CI, and the local gate strictly gains two. Full reversal is deleting two lines from repo.yaml's verify.core.
alternatives: Add `./scripts/ci-go.sh lint` to verify.core and leave ci-go.sh calling a bare `golangci-lint` -- REJECTED: on any machine without a manual install (including this one) the local gate goes red with 'command not found', which is a worse failure than the gap it closes, and trains agents to ignore the gate.

Leave verify.core at four steps and only document in repo.yaml which two steps CI adds and why -- REJECTED, and it is the alternative the acceptance criteria explicitly permit. PR #90 is the evidence against it: the failure mode is an agent trusting a protocol sentence, and a comment in repo.yaml does not reach the agent reading the gate-parity step. Honest documentation of a gap is the fallback for a gap that cannot be closed; this one can be closed for 37s.

Make ci-go.sh always use `go run` and delete the install step from ci.yml, for one code path everywhere -- REJECTED: ci.yml's comment records that source builds were tried in CI and abandoned as network-fragile and slow. Deleting a checksum-verified, content-addressed pin in favour of a sumdb build would trade a stronger pin for a weaker one and re-introduce a known flake.

Install golangci-lint into the dev environment and document the install step in CONTRIBUTING.md -- REJECTED: it makes the local gate's correctness depend on every machine having run a manual setup step nothing verifies. The repo already chose the opposite pattern for govulncheck, and consistency with that precedent is worth more than saving one `go run`.

Add a .golangci.yml to pin the linter SET as well as the linter VERSION -- REJECTED as out of scope. CI enforces the v2 default set today with no config file; introducing one would change which analyses run, which is a different decision from making local and CI run the same ones. Worth a separate item if the default set ever surprises us.

Remove `vuln` and `lint` from the CI core job so the two lists match at four steps -- REJECTED on principle: the skills policy and the deliver protocol both forbid weakening a check to reach green, and this would delete the exact analysis that caught the SA1019 hits.
scope: Gate surface and the docs that describe it: repo.yaml (verify.core plus the comment above it), scripts/ci-go.sh (pinned lint version, linter resolution, lint-version mode), .github/workflows/ci.yml (install step derives its version from ci-go.sh; no job, step, or check removed), .github/pull_request_template.md, .warden/skills-policy.md (Verify section wording), CONTRIBUTING.md (Commands section). No Go source changes, no behaviour change in the library, and nothing under adapters/export/gcp/, docs/adapters.md, README.md, or docs/architecture/, which other agents hold concurrently. .warden/skills-policy.md's Forbidden paths section allows a gate-surface change only in a PR whose tracked item is explicitly about policy or CI: workspace-dfd is that item, and the PR body says so.
